title: Conditional κ = 0.001372550159367980: cross-copy hosting on #472's R715 eleven-stage word (+1.63% over #469)
body:
Conditional **κ = 1372550159367980/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.372550159367980·10⁻³**, bit-bound, **+1.63 % over #469** (1.3505809·10⁻³) and **+6.23 % over #472** (1.2920996·10⁻³). This is #448's cross-copy slot applied to #472's suppliers: chafreaky's R715 word with shared kernel, target mixing and retimings in eleven compressed stages on the bit side, and #448's cross-copy hosted #433 word on the complex side. Neither local word nor any schedule, isometry or bridge changes; only the owners of the helper residuals do.

## Change

#472 hosts all 62,920 helper residual occurrences whole on idle data families (pooling the eight replicas), which leaves copies partly empty because widths 8/7/6 do not tile children of rank 7, 14, 28, 42 and 56; those remainders are paid. Here the pending sets of a child's 1,920 pooled copies form one tape, residuals are laid along it widest first, and a residual that straddles a copy boundary is owned by two copies of the same child, which share the window. The complete-program identity is #448 §2, family by family; the exact finite check of #448 §7 covers the two-family case in the model of #451's note. The concave cost makes the contiguous fill optimal: filled copies pay nothing and only the unfilled copies of the rank-56 final children pay.

| supplier | parent saving | this saving | hosted residuals (split) | max child |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bit, m = 78, R = 715, 11 stages, 8 replicas | 1.293771·10⁻³ (#472) | **1.374423·10⁻³** | 62,920 (14,612) | 56 |
| complex, m = 73, R = 560 | 1.437532·10⁻³ (#448) | 1.437532·10⁻³ | 40,320 (13,720) | 48 |

Accounting follows #472: eleven-stage invoice with three-level halving, complete row bound 19,431 < 20,161, the chronological physical prefix bound recomputed on the new owners (a split owner's two families both receive the update, a new accounting choice that is a review point of its own; 1,161 bits charged 1,216), one further route factor per helper selector for the split. Deficit 3,264 unchanged. The integer programme is frozen in `SELECTION.json`; any residual it leaves out is placed on an in-window child with room.

## Validation

`python3 -B research/cross-copy-hosting-r715/verify.py /absolute/new/output [--quick]` runs #472's complete verifier (which rebuilds #458's complex supplier and the R715 composition), then both generators, an independent audit that shares no code with them (windows re-derived; one owner record per helper; pieces on copies of the named child, inside the pending set, widths summing to the residual width, disjoint per (child, copy), inside the window, off the active pair; owner families recomputed; unchanged template parts byte-identical to #472's; remainders, profile, stock, deficit, emitted-program digest and prefix bits recomputed; fifteen mutation controls rejected), and the exact assembly (two rational moment engines per supplier, both finite invoices, six bootstrap levels, all 47 strict outer inequalities; next-grid and η/β controls rejected). Local run: macOS, Python 3.14, quick mode (skips only #443's inherited exhaustive controls); every value, the emitted digest and the complex template hash match `EXPECTED.json`. CI is not claimed before it runs.

## Scope

Conditional like its parents. The review point is #448's cross-copy slot, on which #450, #453, #464 and #469 also rest; #451's trace note and the replies on that thread describe the disagreement. #472's own review points and all inherited interfaces remain assumptions. No Lean proof and no unconditional integer-multiplication theorem is claimed.
